name: Native Android App (Jetpack Compose & Clean Architecture)
description: Production-ready Android application architecture utilizing Kotlin, Jetpack Compose UI (Material 3), MVVM / MVI unidirectional state flow, Room SQLite database, Coroutines/Flow, Retrofit networking, and Hilt dependency injection.

clarifying_questions.question: State architecture & UI pattern?
options: MVI with Unidirectional Data Flow (StateFlow + SharedFlow)
Clean Architecture 3-tier (Domain UseCases + Data Repositories + UI)
clarifying_questions.impacts: Structures UI State sealed classes, Intent/Event handling, and Repository interfaces

clarifying_questions.question: Data caching & offline strategy?
options: Offline-First (Room DB is Single Source of Truth + Network Sync)
Network-First with HTTP OkHttp Cache fallback
clarifying_questions.impacts: Adds Room DAO Flow queries, WorkManager periodic sync workers, and network bound resource

clarifying_questions.question: Background execution & sync?
clarifying_questions.impacts: Configures AndroidManifest service declarations, battery optimization exemptions, and WorkManager constraints

clarifying_questions.question: Device authentication & storage security?
options: BiometricPrompt (Fingerprint / Face Unlock) + Android Keystore encryption
clarifying_questions.impacts: Adds BiometricManager checks, CryptoObject, and MasterKeys encrypted Datastore

common_stacks: Kotlin + Jetpack Compose + Room + Retrofit + Hilt + Coroutines
known_failure_modes: Triggering network calls or disk I/O on Dispatchers.Main (blocking UI thread causing ANRs) — always switch to Dispatchers.IO
Storing plaintext auth tokens in standard SharedPreferences — use EncryptedSharedPreferences with Android Keystore
Memory leaks from retaining Activity/Context references inside singletons or ViewModels — use Application Context or Hilt ViewModel injection
Failing to handle Android configuration changes (screen rotation, dark mode switch, process death) causing UI state loss — use rememberSaveable and SavedStateHandle
Hardcoding layout sizes in pixels (px) instead of density-independent pixels (dp/sp), causing broken scaling on different phone resolutions
